claims.text: Cryogenic substrate cooling during laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi will reduce thermal gradients.
Cryogenic substrate cooling during laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi will reduce residual stresses.
Cryogenic substrate cooling will improve the mechanical properties of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The feedstock is pre-alloyed, as-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder.
The powder has a uniform particle-size distribution.
The powder has a relaxed oxidation state.
Lower thermal gradients and rapid solidification will produce a refined microstructure.
Cryogenic processing will minimize grain growth.
Cryogenic processing will reduce segregation.
Cryogenic substrate cooling lowers the thermal input during deposition.
Lower thermal input reduces the buildup of residual stresses.
Cryogenic cooling limits overheating-induced defects.
Rapid cooling promotes a fine-grained microstructure.
A fine-grained microstructure enhances overall mechanical performance.
Cryogenically cooled components will have statistically lower residual stresses than conventionally processed components.
Cryogenically cooled components will have higher yield strength than conventionally processed components.
Cryogenically cooled components will have improved ductility relative to conventionally processed components.
Cryogenically cooled components will have a more homogeneous microstructure than conventionally processed components.
Conventional laser powder bed fusion without substrate cooling typically produces high residual stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity because of elevated thermal loads.
The proposed mechanism is applicable primarily to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components processed by inert-atmosphere laser powder bed fusion with substrate-cooling capability.
